pass_b_english: It is as if one is cast down from the foundations, but young men who are recently in their prime are laid in the same manner.
Those who have already attained a safe and truly god-loving mind, and are rooted in faith in God, remain unshaken, even as Satan tempts them.
On the other hand, those who still have a heart that indulges in luxury would easily fall away, unless they often receive corrective words.
If such people were not in my midst, I would have spoken directly to those who are trained.
But since I see many who are undecided, I must address them.
It is time to say to them, as Paul did, "Beware, brothers and sisters, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God." (Hebrews 3:12)
If we must say something openly, let us approach faith without pretence, with a whole heart and mind.
No one can serve two masters, for either they will hate one and love the other, or they will be devoted to one and despise the other.

As we consider the story of someone who was taken captive by barbarians at a young age and raised among them, we see how they adopted the customs and habits of their captors, but also struggled with the ingrained values of their homeland.

As this person grew in understanding and maturity, they began to recognize the truth about their situation and longed for their beloved homeland and desired to be instructed in the paternal laws that had been passed down to them.
Eventually, they presented themselves to the king and stated the reasons for their actions, and as a result, they were deemed worthy of honor and old age.

The question arises, then, whether such a person, still barbarized and thinking like their captors, would reasonably be expected to be punished, or whether they would be worthy of greater things due to their faithfulness and goodwill.
Let us return to the beginning of the human race and examine the things concerning the first-formed man.
He was full of every good and had reached the highest peak of joy within us, of which he was also master, unless he had transgressed the divine commandment out of deception.
The first of the sons born from him, together with him, offered the firstfruits of what they had found, for nature knew how to honor God, needing no law for this.
Abel offered sacrifices from his flock, while Cain did so from the fruits of the earth.
For Abel was a shepherd, and it seemed good to Cain to cultivate the earth, and he did this.

But as the human race always slid towards what is worse, and suffered a more shameful evil than what had gone before, the law that had been sown in nature was destroyed and trampled, although it persuaded God to give the one and only.
Moreover, the error of polytheism was added to all the other evils, a terrible teaching, a peak of the devil's bitterness.
It was thus, and not otherwise, that our affairs were led to complete destruction, and we were excluded from friendship with God due to the sin that was introduced.
As we naturally incline towards God, we fear that we may be shaken off from his greed and drawn to the ancient beauty of our own nature.
However, this desire has been corrupted by false worship, which has clothed humanity in a kind of slavery.
The free person has become a slave, as it were, to the whims of their own desires.
But this deceitful hunt will not succeed, for it is not possible for humanity to reach the end of things according to its own mind.
The cowardly person fights against God out of ignorance, and suffers the same fate as sailors who cling to the winds and are destroyed by their own ship.
In contrast, the only-begotten Word of God has shone upon us, freeing us from the bonds of sin and showing us to be free instead of captives.
This is the ancient and innate knowledge of the one and true God, which has been corrupted by the foreign and harmful invention of worshiping many gods.
We do not pay homage to the sun, moon, stars, earth, and water, for we have been given the name of divinity and have written down a multitude of gods.
Having been redeemed through Christ, we remain faithful and true worshippers of the one who has been honored.
We must not be deceived by empty words, nor have unfaithfulness in our minds, lest we be found to be pretentious outwardly while hiding an idolater within.
If one still has a barbaric mindset, what does it mean to claim royal thoughts?
The law knows the assistant of freedom, not the traitor.
One who genuinely struggles and is unwilling to conquer opponents is not double-minded and abominable.
Even the Greek poets have spoken similarly, and one would agree that it is correct.
However, they are haughty and sacrilegious, and they call themselves by other names, which seems to me to be a beautiful way of thinking.
I have heard one of them say clearly that those who conceive one thing and express another are equal to the gates of Hades.
For deceit and fraud are truly accursed and easily refuted, and they accuse the worst of all vices.
What is the point of silence, and why do you conceal in darkness the things that you hold dear in your mind?
Is it not the case that you are eager to hide, and that this hiding is motivated by the shame that you would feel if your true nature were to be revealed?

For it is characteristic of someone who is trying to hide their flaws to conceal the things for which they would be justly criticized, and to lack the brightness that comes from being open and honest.
If you are aware of the things that are worthy of wonder, and you are sane, then why do you not make yourself known to all, and reveal your true nature?

If you are ashamed of the things that are hidden within you, and you use a veil to conceal the invisible aspects of your character, then you are seeking glory through a false pretense, and this is more honorable than the things that are rightly believed.
Why do you not speak to others about these things, and find yourself radiant and confident, speaking as a brother to those who are inwardly focused, and as a relative to those who are…

   Σατανᾶς. Οἵ γε μὴν ἔτι τρυφᾷν ἔχοντες τὴν καρδίαν, εἰ μὴ σφό δρα συχνὸν
   τὸν ἐπανορθοῦντα δέχοιντο λόγον, εὐκό λως ἂν, οἶμαι, διολισθήσειαν, καὶ
   πρὸς ἅπαν ἠχή σονται τὸ τῷ καταστρέφοντι δοκοῦν. Εἰ μὲν οὖν οὐκ ἦσαν ἐν
   ἐμοὶ οἱ τοιοῦτοι, κἂν εὐθὺς ἐχρῆν ἰθυ δρομῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐπὶ τὰ τῶν
   μαθημάτων ἐξησκη μένα, καὶ τελειοτέραν ἔχοντα τὴν ὑφήγησιν. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ
   πολλοὺς, οἶμαι, κατίδοι τις ἂν, οἷς οὐκ οἶδ' ὅπως ἐπὶ τὸ διαῤῥιπτεῖσθαι φίλον,
   ἐπαμφοτερίζουσάν τε τὴν διάνοιαν ἔχειν πρός τε τὸν φύσει καὶ τοὺς οὐκ
   ὄντας τοῦτο θεοὺς, ἢ καὶ οὕτω κατωνομασμένους, τί τὸ νοσοῦν ἀφέντες,
   ἀβούλως ἐπὶ τὸ μὴ οὕτως ἔχον ἴομεν εὐθύς; Ὥρα τοίνυν, ὡς ἔοικε, κατὰ τὸν

   τινι ὑμῶν καρδία πονηρὰ ἀπιστίας ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ζῶντος." Εἰ
